name: block_diagram
title: Block diagram
shows: The SoC as instantiated in rtl/soc_top.sv and rtl/periph_subsys.sv: core, caches, arbiter, AXI4-Lite master and interconnect, external memory port, APB bridge and the four peripherals.

name: pipeline_hazards
title: Pipeline hazards
shows: A load followed at once by a use of its result: the hazard unit holds IF/ID for one cycle and inserts a bubble into EX; the dependent instruction then takes the loaded value from MEM/WB (fwd_rs1/fwd_rs2).

name: dcache_refill
title: D-cache refill
shows: A load misses in the D-cache: the cache reads the 16-byte line as four single-beat AXI4-Lite reads on the external memory port (one transaction at a time through the arbiter, master and interconnect), then answers the core, which is stalled meanwhile. The I-cache is idle: the loop runs from it.

name: uart_loopback
title: UART loopback
shows: The first byte the program sends ('H', 0x48): start bit, eight data bits LSB first, stop bit, 8 clock cycles per bit; the receiver (TX wired to RX in the testbench) samples each bit in its middle and pushes the byte into the RX FIFO.

name: spi_modes
title: SPI modes 0-3
shows: The first frame in each SPI mode, one panel each: SCLK idles at CPOL; with CPHA = 0 the first bit is on MOSI before the first edge and both sides sample on leading edges, with CPHA = 1 data changes on leading edges and is sampled on trailing ones. The bytes are decoded from the waveform at the sampling edges; MISO comes from the testbench's SPI slave model.

name: cpi_by_model
title: CPI per model
shows: Cycles per instruction of each test on the bare core (single-cycle memory), the core with caches, and the full SoC (caches + AXI4-Lite bus). The tests are short, so cold misses dominate the cached models.
test: every test of the Phase 2/5 suites

name: cache_hit_rates
title: Cache hit rates
shows: Hit rates of the I-cache and of D-cache loads per test, from the hit/miss counters the cache model reports. Tests without data loads show no D-cache bar.
test: every test of the Phase 2 suite

name: uvm_coverage
title: UVM coverage
shows: Coverage bins of the UVM environment for the bus and peripheral subsystem: AXI4-Lite direction x region x response x strobes x AW/W order, UART bit lengths and data, SPI mode x bit order.
test: reg_reset, reg_bitbash, uart_tx, uart_rx, spi, irq, axil_order
config: random latency on the memory port

name: timer_interrupt
title: Timer interrupt
shows: mtime reaches mtimecmp and the CLINT raises MTIP; the core takes the interrupt at the commit point (end of MEM) after the instruction there: mepc becomes the next pc, MIE is cleared, the younger instructions are flushed (bubbles) and fetch is redirected to the handler (mtvec, 0x8000005c). Its line misses in the I-cache and is refilled over the bus, so the handler's first instruction reaches ID 39 cycles after the interrupt is taken.

name: functional_coverage
title: Functional coverage
shows: Hit count of every SVA cover point (forwarding paths, load-use, branch after load, CSR sequences, interrupts during a stall or flush, every exception and interrupt cause, cache corner cases) merged over the regression.
test: the Phase 2 suite on the core and cache models, every SoC and C test

name: regression_dashboard
title: Regression dashboard
shows: Passed and total runs of every regression, each test in each memory configuration and seed, read from the result files of the make targets; and the size of the lockstep comparison against Spike.

name: mutation_checks
title: Mutation checks
shows: Bugs deliberately injected into the RTL, one at a time, and the regression that has to catch each one (scripts/cosim_mutants.py; the co-simulation mutants must also pass the self-checking tests, so only co-simulation can catch them). rtl/ is restored and checksummed after every mutant.
command: make cosim-mutants cache-mutants bus-mutants periph-mutants lockstep-mutants uvm-mutants

name: layout
title: Layout (sky130)
shows: The routed SoC rendered from its final GDS by KLayout: 2.33 mm² die, 41,246 standard cells and 4 SRAM macros; Fmax 52.1 MHz (typical corner). The dashed outlines are the four OpenRAM macros as placed in the routed DEF. Sign-off errors: Magic DRC 0, KLayout DRC 0, LVS 0 (docs/results.md).
